title: Policy engine: deterministic compatibility checks + safe fallback for quantization profiles
creator: Ethan Park
content:
## Context
We’re launching the Quantization Profile Library (opt-in) and need the control-plane policy evaluation to safely resolve a route’s requested quantization profile into a deterministic “applied profile” decision for the runtime.

This ticket implements:
1) deterministic compatibility checks for a candidate profile vs the resolved request context, and
2) safe fallback behavior when incompatible (or when anything is missing/ambiguous).

This is the primary safety boundary between user-config intent (route settings) and runtime execution.

## Problem statement
Without strict compatibility checks, a route can be configured to reference a profile that is:
- incompatible with the model variant actually being served (including pinned version / alias drift)
- incompatible with the GPU class/arch in a region or dedicated pool
- incompatible with runtime capabilities (e.g., FP8 kernels not enabled for a given build)
- unsafe for a context-length / seq-len regime

Additionally, non-deterministic resolution (e.g., depending on cache freshness or registry lookup ordering) can cause request-to-request variance, making debugging impossible and breaking our auditability guarantees.

## Goals / non-goals
### Goals
- Deterministic policy evaluation outcome for a given (route config, model ref, region/tier, runtime capability set).
- Explicit “resolution outcome” surfaced to runtime + telemetry: applied vs fallback vs disabled.
- Safe, conservative fallback to baseline precision (default behavior) when any incompatibility is detected.
- Guardrail behavior consistent across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

### Non-goals
- Automatic per-customer profile recommendations.
- Auto-tuning or auto-switching profiles based on live traffic.
- Default-on enablement.

## Definitions
- **quantization_profile_ref**: route-level config value. Can be “default” (off) or a concrete profile reference.
- **Resolved profile**: policy output after validation/compat checks (may be null if fallback/disabled).
- **Compatibility context**: inputs to checks: model_id + variant, model version, GPU SKU class, region, deployment tier, max_context, runtime capability flags.

## Proposed approach
### 1) Deterministic resolution contract
Policy evaluation must be a pure function over:
- Route config snapshot (including quantization_profile_ref)
- Model resolution snapshot (model_id, variant, pinned version if applicable)
- Execution context (region, deployment tier/capacity pool, gpu_sku_class)
- Policy-engine build/runtime capability set (e.g., supports_fp8_mixed_path=true)
- Global kill-switch / tenant-level disable (if present in config)

No “best effort” partial application: if required compatibility inputs cannot be resolved, we must fallback.

### 2) Compatibility checks (blocklist style)
For a candidate profile, fail compatibility if any of the following are true:
- **Model mismatch**: profile.model_id != resolved_model.model_id OR profile.variant != resolved_model.variant.
- **Profile status**: profile.status in {deprecated, blocked} (or profile.expiration passed).
- **Hardware mismatch**: gpu_sku_class not in profile.hardware_constraints.allowed_gpu_classes.
- **Runtime capability mismatch**: profile.quant_method requires capabilities not present (e.g., fp8 kernels, int8 act quant support).
- **Context constraints**: resolved max_context > profile.constraints.max_context (or request context-length regime violates constraints).
- **Known caveats**: profile.caveats contains “no-determinism-risk” or “unstable-kv-cache” flagged as hard-block for v1.

Notes:
- For v1, treat missing fields in profile constraints as conservative: missing constraint == incompatible unless explicitly documented as optional in schema.
- We will not implement “partial compat” (e.g., allow up to N context) in policy. Either compatible or fallback.

### 3) Fallback behavior
If incompatible (or config is invalid), policy returns:
- quantization_enabled=false
- quant_profile_id=null
- resolution_outcome="fallback"
- resolution_reason=one_of(enum)

Fallback means baseline precision/default kernels. No retries, no loops.

### 4) Observability outputs (must be stable)
Emit structured decision fields (to routing/runtime headers and metrics dimensions):
- quantization.requested_ref (string)
- quantization.resolved_profile_id (string or empty)
- quantization.outcome: applied | fallback | disabled
- quantization.reason: disabled_by_config | kill_switch | model_mismatch | hw_incompatible | runtime_capability_missing | context_incompatible | profile_blocked | profile_not_found | invalid_ref

### 5) Caching and lookup semantics
- Policy engine may consult the Model Registry for profile metadata, but the decision must be deterministic given the cached snapshot.
- Cache key must include the exact profile_id + version (not “latest”) to avoid silent changes.
- If route config uses an alias (e.g., “recommended”), policy must resolve alias -> pinned profile version deterministically at write time (preferred) or at evaluation time with explicit “resolved_version” recorded. (See open question below.)

## Open questions
1) Do we allow non-versioned aliases (“recommended/latest”) in route config for v1?
   - Proposal: allow aliases only if they resolve to a specific versioned profile in the config service at write time (so evaluation is stable). If not, block enablement and require explicit version.

## Implementation plan
- Add CompatContext struct to policy engine (region, tier, gpu_sku_class, model_id/variant/version, max_context, capability flags).
- Implement profile lookup + schema validation error handling: profile_not_found / invalid_profile.
- Implement check pipeline in fixed order; first failure wins and sets resolution_reason.
- Ensure no fallback loop: evaluation should never re-enter profile selection after deciding fallback.
- Add unit tests for each reason + determinism test (same inputs => same outputs).
- Add integration test with config service + model registry cache behavior under QPS.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Compatibility checks exist for model/variant, GPU class, runtime capability flags, and context-length constraints.
- [x] Policy evaluation returns deterministic outcome fields and stable resolution_reason.
- [x] Any incompatibility leads to baseline fallback without retries/loops.
- [x] Metrics dimensions and log fields are populated to support dashboards: applied rate, fallback rate, reason breakdown.
- [x] Unit tests cover all failure modes + “missing field” conservatism.
- [x] Integration test demonstrates no thundering herd (cache hit expected) and deterministic alias behavior (or alias blocked).

## Links
- ADR: adr-0137-route-level-quantization-profile-enablement
- Serving standard: quantization-profile-compatibility-and-fallbacks
- Related tickets: ENG-5814 (route config field), ENG-5819 (global kill-switch), ENG-5817 (dashboards)

## Notes for rollout
- Keep default behavior unchanged when field is unset or set to “default”.
- Ensure fallback reason is visible in internal traces for debugging design partner rollouts.
- Coordinate with SRE on alert thresholds for fallback_rate spikes (could indicate profile publication issue or registry outage).
comments: 2025-01-27 (Jordan Lee): Drafted compat check order + reason enum. Biggest risk is alias semantics (“recommended/latest”) causing silent changes; leaning toward resolving to versioned ID at write-time in config service. Looping in Ethan/Benji.

2025-02-03 (Ravi Menon): Please ensure we include deployment tier (hosted/dedicated/private) in the compat context. Dedicated pools have mixed SKUs behind a pool name; we should normalize to gpu_sku_class so we don’t bake in per-SKU lists everywhere.

2025-02-06 (Benji Okafor): Config service can resolve aliases on write and store a fully qualified profile_id@version. That keeps policy pure. Will add a validation endpoint so Console can show why an alias can’t be resolved.

2025-02-12 (Mina Haddad): Add a guard for max_context mismatch. We saw routes with 8k defaults but some profiles only validated for 4k; fallback reason should be explicit so oncall can triage quickly.

2025-02-20 (Jordan Lee): Implemented CompatContext + check pipeline behind feature flag. Added determinism unit test: freeze mock registry snapshot + assert stable decision across 1k iterations. Next: integration test w/ registry cache + rate limit protection.
2025-03-04 (Jordan Lee): Fixed edge case: profile_not_found previously returned invalid_ref; now distinct. Also ensured no secondary lookup after a failure (prevents fallback loops).
2025-03-11 (Connor O'Brien): For release readiness: we need fallback reason wired to dashboards. Please confirm metric tag names align with ENG-5817 panels: outcome + reason breakdown.
2025-03-18 (Jordan Lee): Landed + verified in perf-canary env. Fallback loop regression test added. Alias is resolved at write-time (blocked if cannot resolve to concrete version). Marking Done.
